landing.meta_description: Track your whole investment portfolio in one place: import DeGiro, Trading 212, Interactive Brokers, MyInvestor and more. True returns (TWR), FIFO cost basis, rebalancing and a tax report. Free.
landing.hero_subtitle: Consolidate DeGiro, Trading 212, IBKR, MyInvestor and Binance —and any other broker via AI— in a single panel. Real returns, FIFO cost basis and an annual tax report. All free.
landing.pain_subtitle: Investors with multiple brokers waste hours every month trying to consolidate data that should be in one place.
landing.pain_0_body: Your positions are spread across your broker, your index fund and your exchange. Seeing the real total means copying, pasting and hoping.
landing.pain_1_body: Monthly contributions inflate the number. Without TWR, you can't tell if you gained from skill or from adding more money.
landing.pain_2_body: How much of your gain was the asset and how much was EUR/USD? Without FX decomposition, you'll never know.

landing.how_1_body: TWR, FIFO P&L, monthly breakdown and Portfolio Score. Everything calculated instantly.
landing.how_2_body: Use rebalancing, the AI chat or the compound calculator to act on real data.

landing.method_quote: Simple return inflates with every contribution you make. TWR cancels that out and measures only your decisions — the same yardstick funds use to report results.
landing.method_note: It's maths, not marketing. That's why you won't find invented testimonials or filler numbers here — just the method.

landing.security_subtitle: Privacy and security by design, not as an afterthought.
landing.security_0_title: Encryption at rest and in transit
landing.security_0_body: All your data travels encrypted with TLS and is stored encrypted at rest. On top of that, every database row is isolated per user (Supabase RLS): no query can reach someone else's portfolio.
landing.security_1_body: Trazza only reads the files you upload yourself. We never ask for your broker credentials and never connect directly to your accounts.
landing.security_2_body: Data stored in Europe. Right to access, rectify and delete guaranteed at all times.
landing.security_3_body: Your financial data is yours. We never sell or share it with third parties. Ever.
landing.faq_0_a: Yes, completely free during beta. No credit card, no surprises. When we leave beta the core features will remain available at no cost.
landing.faq_1_a: DeGiro, Trading 212, Interactive Brokers (IBKR) and MyInvestor have direct import: pick the broker, upload its export and it runs through its native parser. Binance exports are also recognised automatically when pasted or dropped in, without spending AI quota. And any other broker works through AI import: paste the text, a screenshot or a PDF and the AI structures it for you.
landing.faq_2_a: You export your broker history, upload the file and Trazza validates it automatically, detecting duplicates and errors before saving. The process takes less than 2 minutes.
landing.faq_3_a: Your data is stored on European servers with encryption at rest and in transit. Trazza never asks for direct access to your broker accounts — only the files you choose to upload. If you use an AI feature, whatever you send at that moment is processed by our AI provider; it is all spelled out in the privacy policy.
landing.faq_4_q: What is the difference between TWR and simple return?
landing.faq_4_a: Simple return is inflated by contributions. TWR (Time-Weighted Return) neutralises that effect and shows the real return of your investment decisions, regardless of when or how much you contributed.
landing.faq_5_q: Can I use it for my tax return?
landing.faq_5_a: Trazza generates an annual tax report with your realized gains and losses (FIFO method), net dividends received and fees, exportable to CSV. It is indicative — not tax advice: always cross-check with your broker's tax certificates before filing.
landing.feat_10_body: Reorder, hide or pair the dashboard widgets. Your setup is saved: next time you log in, it is exactly as you left it.
landing.feat_11_body: When a company you hold reports, the AI explains what happened and how the market reacted. Without reading the whole presentation.

calc_page.title: Compound Interest Calculator — Trazza
calc_page.meta: Free compound interest calculator: simulate how your investment grows with periodic contributions, compounding and annual return. Chart and year-by-year breakdown.
calc_page.intro: Simulate your investment's growth with the power of compound interest. Adjust the initial capital, periodic contribution, annual return and time horizon, and watch it build up year by year.
calc_page.explainer_1: Compound interest is the interest you earn not only on your initial capital, but also on the interest accumulated in previous periods. Reinvesting those returns makes your money grow exponentially, not linearly — and the effect snowballs the longer your time horizon.
calc_page.explainer_2: That's why time is your biggest ally: a steady contribution over many years often matters more than the exact amount you put in. Use this calculator to see the real impact of starting earlier and staying consistent.
calc_page.cta_title: From simulation to your real portfolio
calc_page.cta_body: When you sign in to Trazza, the calculator pre-loads with your real portfolio value. Consolidate your brokers and measure your true return with TWR and FIFO.

div_calc.title: Dividend calculator: your net income as a Spanish tax resident — Trazza
div_calc.meta: Work out what you really keep from your dividends as a Spanish tax resident: withholding by country, 2025 savings tax brackets and the double-taxation deduction. Free.
div_calc.intro: What you really keep from your dividends after the source-country withholding and Spanish income tax, and how much is lost along the way if you don’t reclaim it.
div_calc.explainer_1: Gross dividends are the amount invested times the dividend yield. The company’s country withholds part at source (the US 15% with the W-8BEN form), and in Spain dividends are taxed in the savings base by brackets: 19% to 30% for the 2025 tax year. To avoid paying twice, you can deduct the foreign withholding up to the tax-treaty limit, usually 15%.
div_calc.explainer_2: Anything withheld above that 15% is not recovered in your Spanish return: you have to reclaim it from that country, which is why a Swiss (35%) or German (26.375%) dividend ends up yielding less than a US one. If you have other savings income that year (gains on sales, interest), add it: it pushes your dividends into a higher bracket.
div_calc.cta_title: Your real dividends, from every broker
div_calc.cta_body: Trazza imports the dividends you received from DeGiro, Trading 212, Interactive Brokers and MyInvestor, with their withholding, and groups them in each year’s tax report.
div_calc.f_yield_hint: For example, 3% if a €100 share pays €3 a year.
div_calc.f_other_hint: Gains on sales, interest… They set your tax bracket. If you have none, leave it at 0.
div_calc.r_effective: In total you pay {{rate}}% tax on the gross amount.
div_calc.r_lost: The source country withholds more than the treaty lets you deduct: {{amount}} a year is not recovered in your return. You can reclaim it from that country, but it’s a separate process.
div_calc.disclaimer: Indicative calculation for a Spanish tax resident using the {{year}} savings tax brackets. Each country’s withholding may vary with your situation and broker. Not a substitute for professional tax advice.

fire_calc.title: FIRE calculator: how much you need and when you get there — Trazza
fire_calc.meta: Work out your FIRE number with the 4% rule and how many years until financial independence from your savings, monthly contribution and return. Free.
fire_calc.intro: How much you need invested to live off your investments, and how many years it takes with what you save today.
fire_calc.explainer_title: What FIRE is and the 4% rule
fire_calc.explainer_1: FIRE (financial independence, retire early) means having enough invested for your portfolio to pay your expenses. The classic reference is the 4% rule: withdrawing 4% of the portfolio each year has historically lasted about 30 years. So your target is your annual expenses divided by the withdrawal rate: 25 times your expenses at 4%, about 28.6 times at 3.5%.
fire_calc.explainer_2: The calculator works in today’s euros: the return you enter should be real, net of inflation (4–5% is a prudent reference for a global equity portfolio). That way expenses and the target don’t need inflating. If you plan to retire for more than 30 years, a 3–3.5% rate gives more margin.
fire_calc.cta_title: Track your path to FIRE with real data
fire_calc.cta_body: Trazza brings all your brokers together and tells you your portfolio’s real return, so your plan starts from your numbers, not an example.
fire_calc.f_expenses_hint: What you spend (or expect to spend) per year once you stop working.
fire_calc.f_return_hint: Net of inflation. 4–5% is a prudent reference.
fire_calc.f_wr_hint: The classic rule is 4%. For more than 30 years, 3–3.5%.
fire_calc.r_no_target: Enter a withdrawal rate above 0 to calculate it.
fire_calc.r_never_hint: With these numbers the portfolio never reaches the target. Try raising the monthly contribution or lowering expenses.
fire_calc.chart_aria: Portfolio value over time versus money contributed and the target
fire_calc.disclaimer: Simulation with a constant return; markets don’t move in a straight line. Indicative only, not investment advice.

common.declare_title: How to report it on your Spanish tax return
common.basics_title: The basics that apply to any broker
common.fifo_body: When you sell part of a holding bought in several lots, the Spanish tax agency treats the first shares bought as the first ones sold (FIFO). The gain is the sale price minus the cost of those first lots, including buy and sell commissions. The average price shown in your broker app does not count.
common.rates_body: Gains, dividends and interest go to the savings tax base. For the 2025 return it is taxed at 19% up to €6,000, 21% up to €50,000, 23% up to €200,000, 27% up to €300,000 and 30% above that. Losses offset gains of the same year and, within limits, of the next four.
common.two_months_body: If you sell listed shares or ETFs at a loss and buy the same securities within the two months before or after, that loss cannot be claimed yet: it is deferred until you definitively sell the shares that blocked it (without buying the same security again within the two months before or after that sale).
common.disclaimer: Informational guide, not tax advice. Rules and tax return boxes change every year: check your case with the Spanish tax agency or an adviser before filing.

index.title: How to report your investments on your Spanish tax return, broker by broker — Trazza
index.meta: Guides to export your DEGIRO, Interactive Brokers, Trading 212, MyInvestor and Binance transactions and report them on your Spanish tax return: FIFO, dividends, withholding and forms 720/721.
index.h1: Export and report your investments, broker by broker
index.intro: Every broker exports its data differently and not all of them report to the Spanish tax agency. For each one, here is where to download your transactions and what to do with them on your tax return.

degiro.title: DEGIRO: how to export your transactions and report them in Spain — Trazza
degiro.meta: Download the DEGIRO Account statement, calculate your gains with FIFO and report sales, dividends and withholding on your Spanish tax return. Includes Form 720.
degiro.card: Foreign broker: no withholding and nothing in your draft return. How to get the Account statement and what to report.
degiro.h1: DEGIRO: export your transactions and report them on your tax return
degiro.intro: DEGIRO is a foreign broker: it does not withhold Spanish income tax and your transactions do not reach your draft return. You have to calculate gains and dividends yourself and add them by hand.
degiro.fact_entity: flatexDEGIRO Bank AG (Germany), a non-resident entity in Spain.
degiro.fact_withholding: No Spanish withholding. Foreign dividends arrive with the source-country withholding.
degiro.fact_draft: Its sales and dividends usually do not appear: you add them by hand.
degiro.fact_model: Form 720 if your foreign securities exceed €50,000 on 31 December (cash counts separately, with the same threshold).
export_steps: Log in to DEGIRO on the web (not the mobile app).
Pick a date range starting the day you opened the account: without the full history, the FIFO cost of what you sell will be wrong.
Click Download and choose CSV. The file is called Account.csv.
degiro.export_note: The «Transactions» export is not enough: it lacks dividends, commissions and cash movements. For a complete portfolio you need the Account statement.
declare: Share and ETF sales: section F2 of Renta Web (transfer of listed shares), with the sale and purchase values in euros. Buy commissions add to the cost and sell commissions reduce the proceeds.
Dividends: the gross amount, in euros, in box 0029.
Tax withheld by the source country (e.g. 15% in the US) is recovered as the international double taxation deduction in box 0588, up to the treaty limit.
Transactions in dollars or other currencies: convert each amount to euros at the exchange rate of its date.
pitfalls: Reporting the net dividend instead of the gross amount.
Forgetting buy and sell commissions, which reduce the gain.
Using the average price from the app instead of the FIFO cost.
Selling at a loss and buying the same security back within two months.
degiro.trazza: Trazza reads the DEGIRO Account.csv with its own importer: it rebuilds your positions, dividends and commissions, calculates the FIFO cost and your real return, and gives you a yearly tax report you can export to CSV to check against your return.

ibkr.title: Interactive Brokers: export transactions and report them in Spain — Trazza
ibkr.meta: How to download your Interactive Brokers (IBKR) history and report sales, dividends, interest and withholding on your Spanish tax return. FIFO and Form 720.
ibkr.card: Foreign broker with lots of multi-currency activity. How to export the history and convert everything to euros.
ibkr.h1: Interactive Brokers: export your transactions and report them on your tax return
ibkr.intro: Interactive Brokers (IBKR) does not withhold Spanish income tax or report your transactions to the Spanish tax agency. With multi-currency accounts, the hard part is converting every transaction to euros.
ibkr.fact_entity: Interactive Brokers Ireland Ltd (Ireland) for clients resident in Spain: a non-resident entity.
ibkr.fact_withholding: No Spanish withholding. Foreign dividends arrive with the source-country withholding.
ibkr.fact_draft: Nothing from IBKR appears in your draft: sales, dividends and interest are added by hand.
ibkr.fact_model: Form 720 if your foreign securities exceed €50,000 on 31 December (cash counts separately, with the same threshold).
export_steps: Log in to the IBKR portal on the web.
Go to Performance & Reports → Transaction History.
Pick the full period, since you opened the account.
ibkr.export_note: To check figures, IBKR also offers the yearly activity statement and Flex reports. The cost you report must come from a FIFO calculation in euros.
declare: Share and ETF sales: section F2 of Renta Web (transfer of listed shares), sale and purchase values in euros, with commissions.
Dividends: the gross amount in euros in box 0029; foreign withholding as the international double taxation deduction in box 0588, up to the treaty limit.
Interest on cash: income from movable capital, also in the savings base.
Each buy and sell in dollars is converted to euros at the rate of its date: the currency move is part of your gain or loss.
pitfalls: Subtracting the buy and sell prices in dollars and converting only the result.
Forgetting the interest IBKR pays on cash.
Exporting only the last year: without the old purchases, the FIFO cost does not add up.
Buying back within two months a security sold at a loss.
ibkr.trazza: Trazza imports the IBKR history with its own importer: it brings your positions together even across currencies, calculates the FIFO cost and your real return, and gives you a yearly tax report you can export to CSV to check against your return.

t212.title: Trading 212: export your history and report it in Spain — Trazza
t212.meta: How to export your Trading 212 history (all categories, year by year) and report sales, dividends and interest on your Spanish tax return. FIFO, Pies and Form 720.
t212.card: Foreign broker: one year at most per export. How to get the full history and what to report.
t212.h1: Trading 212: export your history and report it on your tax return
t212.intro: Trading 212 does not withhold Spanish income tax and its transactions do not reach your draft return. Each export also covers one year at most, so it is worth pulling the full history carefully.
t212.fact_withholding: No Spanish withholding. Foreign dividends arrive with the source-country withholding.
t212.fact_draft: Its sales, dividends and interest do not appear in your draft: add them by hand.
t212.fact_model: Form 720 if your foreign securities exceed €50,000 on 31 December.
export_steps: Open the menu and go to History.
Click Export and tick every category: orders, dividends, transactions and interest.
Pick the period. Each export covers one year at most, so repeat it year by year since you opened the account.
t212.export_note: If the beginning of the account history is missing, the cost of your first purchases and your cash balance will not add up. Export every year, even if it takes several files.
declare: Share and ETF sales: section F2 of Renta Web, with sale and purchase values in euros. Purchases inside a Pie are real purchases and enter FIFO like any other.
Dividends: the gross amount in euros in box 0029; foreign withholding as the international double taxation deduction in box 0588.
Interest on uninvested cash: income from movable capital.
Transactions in another currency: convert each amount to euros at the rate of its date.
pitfalls: Exporting only the last year and losing the cost of older purchases.
Forgetting the sales a Pie makes when it rebalances: they are taxable too.
Reporting the net dividend instead of the gross amount.
Not reporting interest on cash.
t212.trazza: Trazza imports Trading 212 CSVs with its own importer. You can upload each year's file one after another: it skips repeated movements, calculates the FIFO cost and your real return, and gives you a yearly tax report you can export to CSV.

myinvestor.title: MyInvestor: export your movements and report them in Spain — Trazza
myinvestor.meta: MyInvestor is a Spanish bank: it withholds and reports to the tax agency. How to export your movements, review your draft and report funds, transfers, shares and dividends.
myinvestor.card: Spanish bank: it withholds and reports to the tax agency. What to check in your draft and how fund transfers work.
myinvestor.h1: MyInvestor: export your movements and report them on your tax return
myinvestor.intro: MyInvestor is a Spanish entity: it withholds on dividends and fund redemptions and reports to the tax agency, so much of it appears in your tax data. Your job is to review it, especially the cost of what you sell.
myinvestor.fact_entity: MyInvestor Banco, S.A., a Spanish bank.
myinvestor.fact_withholding: Withholds 19% on dividends and on the gain from fund redemptions.
myinvestor.fact_draft: Reports to the tax agency: dividends, interest and redemptions usually appear in your tax data. Review them before confirming.
myinvestor.fact_model: No Form 720 for MyInvestor: it is a Spanish entity.
export_steps: Funds, shares and ETFs: My portfolio → Transactions → Export CSV.
Robo-advisor portfolios: Managed portfolio → Managed account details → Movements summary → EXCEL.
You can also copy the text from the portfolio screen and paste it into the Trazza importer.
myinvestor.export_note: Export from the start of the account. If you transferred funds from another entity, the original cost travels with the transfer: check it in each fund's details.
declare: Transfers between funds: not taxed. The cost and holding period of the source fund pass to the destination fund.
Fund redemption: capital gain or loss. The 19% already withheld is deducted on your return.
Shares and ETFs: taxed when you sell, with FIFO cost, as with any broker. Check that the sale shows the right purchase cost.
Dividends: the gross amount in box 0029; the Spanish withholding already appears in your tax data and is deducted automatically.
pitfalls: Thinking a transfer is a sale and reporting it.
Confirming the draft without checking the purchase cost of what you sold.
Forgetting that ETFs are taxed like shares: they cannot be transferred tax-free.
Not reporting sales of foreign shares with source withholding.
myinvestor.trazza: Trazza reads MyInvestor movements with its own importer (CSV, Excel or the pasted portfolio text), gives funds readable names, calculates the FIFO cost and your real return, and gives you a yearly tax report to check against your tax data.

binance.title: Binance: download your history and report crypto in Spain — Trazza
binance.meta: Binance stopped serving Spain on 1 July 2026. How to download your history and report sales, swaps and staking on your Spanish tax return, plus Form 721.
binance.card: No longer operates in Spain (MiCA, July 2026), but the past must be reported. How to download your history in time.
binance.h1: Binance: download your history and report your crypto
binance.intro: Since 1 July 2026 Binance no longer serves residents of Spain: it did not obtain the European MiCA licence. You can no longer trade, but you can withdraw your funds and download your history. And everything you traded before must still be reported.
binance.fact_entity: Crypto exchange. It operated in Spain through a Spanish subsidiary until 30 June 2026.
binance.fact_draft: While it had a Spanish subsidiary it reported balances and transactions to the tax agency. That does not exempt you from reporting your gains.
binance.fact_model: Form 721 if your crypto held with foreign custodians exceeds €50,000 on 31 December.
export_steps: Log in to Binance on the web.
Buys and sells: Orders → Spot Order → Trade History → Export. Each report covers one year at most.
Deposits, withdrawals and conversions: Assets → Transaction History → Export.
Download the CSVs and keep them: the download link expires after a few days.
binance.export_note: Download it as soon as possible. You no longer have service from Spain and your history is the proof of your transactions for the tax agency.
declare: Every sale for euros and every swap of one crypto for another (e.g. BTC for ETH) is a capital gain or loss: report it in the virtual currencies section of F2 in Renta Web.
The cost is calculated with FIFO and in euros. USDT or dollar pairs are converted to euros at the rate of each transaction's date.
Staking and Earn: income from movable capital in the year you receive it, per the Spanish Directorate General of Taxes (ruling V1766-22).
If your crypto with foreign custodians exceeded €50,000 on 31 December, file Form 721 (deadline 31 March).
pitfalls: Thinking that swapping one crypto for another is not taxable.
Reporting in USDT without converting amounts to euros.
Not downloading your history before closing the account.
Forgetting staking or Earn rewards.
binance.trazza: Trazza imports your Binance trade history (pairs against USDT, EUR or USD), combines it with the rest of your portfolio and calculates the FIFO cost and your real return.

cg_calc.title: Capital gains calculator for shares with FIFO and the two-month rule (Spain) — Trazza
cg_calc.meta: Calculate the gain or loss on your share and ETF sales for free and without signing up: FIFO cost, commissions, the two-month rule and Spanish income tax brackets for 2025.
cg_calc.h1: Capital gains calculator: what you really make when you sell
cg_calc.intro: Enter your buys and sells and see, sale by sale, the gain or loss the Spanish tax agency expects: FIFO cost with commissions, the two-month rule and your income tax by bracket.
cg_calc.explainer_title: How the Spanish tax agency calculates your gain
cg_calc.explainer_1: When you sell part of a holding bought in several lots, the first shares bought are treated as the first ones sold (FIFO). The gain is the sale amount, minus its commission, minus what those first shares cost including the buy commission. That is why the average price shown by your broker does not work.
cg_calc.explainer_2: If you sell at a loss and buy the same security in the two months before or after, that loss cannot be claimed yet: it is deferred until you definitively sell the repurchased shares (without buying the same security again in the two months before or after). The calculator spots it, defers only the proportional part if you buy back fewer shares, and adds it when you definitively sell what you bought back.
cg_calc.cta_title: Get this calculated automatically from your real trades
cg_calc.cta_body: In Trazza you import your broker statement and get FIFO cost, real return and a yearly tax report without typing a single trade.
cg_calc.ops_hint: One row per buy or sell, in euros. You can mix several securities: each one gets its own FIFO.
cg_calc.invalid: {{count}} incomplete row(s) are left out (missing date, quantity or price).
cg_calc.oversold: You sell {{qty}} more shares than you had bought before this date: their cost counts as zero.
cg_calc.f_other_hint: Dividends and interest: they push your gain into a higher bracket.
cg_calc.no_sales: Add at least one sale to see the result.
cg_calc.loss_sub: Net loss: no tax on these sales and you can offset it.
cg_calc.still_deferred: {{amount}} of deferred losses remain: they will count when you definitively sell the shares that blocked them (without buying again within the two months around that sale).
cg_calc.deferred_note: {{amount}} of this loss is deferred: you bought the same security on {{dates}}, within two months.
cg_calc.released_note: {{amount}} of deferred losses are claimed by selling the shares that blocked them.
cg_calc.disclaimer: Indicative estimate, not tax advice. It does not include other gains of the year or offsets from previous years. Amounts in euros: convert foreign-currency trades at the rate of their date.

renta_calc.title: Calculate DEGIRO capital gains from the CSV for your Spanish tax return, no sign-up — Trazza
renta_calc.meta: Upload DEGIRO's transactions CSV and calculate, free, without signing up and without the file leaving your browser, the gain or loss on each sale: FIFO, fees and a two-month-rule warning.
renta_calc.eyebrow: Free tool · no sign-up · in your browser
renta_calc.h1: Calculate your DEGIRO capital gains for the Spanish tax return from its CSV
renta_calc.intro: Upload the transactions file DEGIRO exports and see, sale by sale, the gain or loss in euros with FIFO cost, fees included, and which losses are deferred by the two-month rule. The file never leaves your device.
renta_calc.explainer_title: What it does with your CSV
renta_calc.explainer_1: It reads each buy and sell in DEGIRO's transactions CSV and takes the euro amount DEGIRO calculated (the Value column, which for foreign-currency trades applies its exchange rate). The purchase fee adds to the cost and the sale fee is subtracted from the proceeds (art. 35 of the Spanish Income Tax Act). When you sell part of a holding bought in several lots, you are deemed to sell what you bought first (FIFO, art. 37.2).
renta_calc.explainer_2: If you sell at a loss and buy the same security in the two months before or after, that loss cannot be included yet (art. 33.5.f): the tool flags it and defers it until you definitively sell what you bought back. Sales of shares and ETFs are reported in section F2 of the Spanish return.
renta_calc.cta_title: Track your whole portfolio, not just one year
renta_calc.cta_body: In Trazza you import DEGIRO's account statement and follow your portfolio with FIFO cost and real returns, alongside your other brokers.
renta_calc.privacy_title: Your file never leaves your device.
renta_calc.privacy_body: The CSV is read and calculated in your browser: it is not sent to Trazza or anyone else, it is not stored, and it is gone when you close or reload the page.
renta_calc.upload_hint: It is the Transactions export, not the Account statement. Export from the date of your first purchase so FIFO has every purchase.
renta_calc.example_loaded: Loaded a made-up sample CSV (not real trades).
renta_calc.error_read: The file could not be read.
renta_calc.error_not_transactions: This does not look like DEGIRO's transactions CSV: the header with Date, ISIN, Quantity and Value is missing.
renta_calc.error_account_file: This is the Account statement (Account.csv). This tool needs the Transactions export.
renta_calc.skipped_date: {{count}} row(s) without a valid date are left out.
renta_calc.skipped_qty: {{count}} row(s) without a quantity are left out.
renta_calc.skipped_not_eur: {{count}} row(s) without a euro amount are left out (account in another currency).
renta_calc.skipped_fee_not_eur: {{count}} row(s) with the fee in another currency are left out.
renta_calc.skipped_no_value: {{count}} row(s) without an amount are left out.
renta_calc.oversold: {{count}} sale(s) sell more shares than were bought earlier in the file: history is missing and those shares count at zero cost. Export from your first purchase.
renta_calc.no_sales: The file has no sales: there are no capital gains to calculate.
renta_calc.disclaimer: Indicative estimate, not tax advice. It uses the euro amounts in DEGIRO's CSV. It does not include other gains of the year or losses carried forward. Check the tax data the Agencia Tributaria provides.
renta_calc.limit_eur: Euro accounts only. For foreign-currency trades it uses the exchange rate DEGIRO applied, which may differ from the one you would use for each date.
renta_calc.limit_degiro: DEGIRO only for now. It does not read Binance or other brokers.
renta_calc.limit_isin: It groups by ISIN and does not classify the type of security: it does not tell funds, ETFs, shares or other products apart, nor apply special rules (fund transfers, rights, splits).
renta_calc.limit_history: FIFO only sees the purchases included in the file.
renta_calc.limit_other: The two-month rule is applied as for listed securities; unlisted securities are not covered.
renta_calc.src_lirpf: Spanish Income Tax Act 35/2006 (BOE), arts. 33.5.f, 35 and 37.2
renta_calc.src_aeat_f2: Agencia Tributaria, 2025 tax return manual: section F2
renta_calc.src_aeat_2m: Agencia Tributaria, 2025 tax return manual: deferred losses
renta_calc.error_too_big: The file is larger than 20 MB: it does not look like a DEGIRO transactions CSV.
renta_calc.error_malformed: The CSV is malformed: there are misplaced quotes (never closed or in the middle of a field). Export it again from DEGIRO without editing it.
renta_calc.incomplete_title: {{count}} security(ies) not calculated: some of their rows could not be read.
renta_calc.incomplete_all: No security is calculated: some skipped rows have no ISIN, so it is unknown which security they belong to.
renta_calc.incomplete_why: Without all their trades FIFO would pick the wrong lots and the two-month rule would not see every purchase, so the result would be wrong. Check those rows in the file.
renta_calc.incomplete_total: Totals exclude the securities that were not calculated.
